rows.selection_reason: No experiments have been completed, so there is zero evidence and maximum uncertainty across all design dimensions (modality, encoder, profile setting, aggregation, fusion). The best first experiment is the simplest possible baseline: RNA-only, single profile, PCA-2000 encoder (config_001). This establishes a clean reference accuracy for the RNA signal alone with a standard, well-understood encoder and no aggregation/fusion complexity. It isolates the contribution of the RNA modality without confounding from learned encoders, multiprofile aggregation, or image fusion. With 9 experiments remaining, this baseline lets me subsequently test (a) whether image-only or multimodal configurations beat RNA-only, (b) whether learned encoders (scvi, scgpt) improve over PCA, and (c) whether multiprofile aggregation adds value. Starting with the simplest configuration maximizes the information gained per experiment by anchoring all future comparisons to a well-defined reference point.

Evidence: config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) achieved only 48.5% accuracy, a weak baseline that leaves major uncertainty about which modality or representation will drive performance. Question: Does the image modality carry useful signal for this task? config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) is the cleanest single-modality comparison to config_001—same profile setting (singleprofile), no aggregation or fusion needed—so any accuracy difference can be attributed primarily to the modality switch. Why this is the best next step: With 8 experiments remaining, knowing whether image features are informative at all is the highest-leverage uncertainty to resolve. If image_only substantially outperforms RNA-only, we should prioritize multimodal and image-heavy configurations; if it is comparable or worse, we can focus the remaining budget on RNA encoder upgrades (scvi, scgpt) and multiprofile aggregation. This single experiment partitions the 51-config space into two very different search strategies.

Evidence: RNA-only with PCA (config_001) achieves 0.485 accuracy while image-only with ResNet50 (config_010) is far weaker at 0.208, establishing RNA as the dominant modality. The key uncertainty is whether the simple linear PCA encoder is a bottleneck or whether a powerful pre-trained single-cell encoder (scGPT) can substantially improve representation quality. This experiment (config_007: RNA-only, single profile, scGPT) isolates the encoder effect while holding profile setting constant at single profile, directly comparing a learned generative pre-trained representation against PCA. If scGPT significantly exceeds 0.485, it justifies investing remaining budget in scGPT-based multimodal and multiprofile configurations; if it does not, PCA is sufficient and we should pivot to testing aggregation/multiprofile or multimodal fusion. With 7 experiments remaining, resolving the encoder question early maximizes information for subsequent choices.

Evidence: PCA (pca_n2000) with singleprofile RNA is the best configuration so far (acc=0.485), outperforming scgpt RNA (0.411) and image-only ResNet50 (0.208). The image modality appears weak, so the most promising direction is improving the RNA pipeline. Uncertainty: We have not yet tested whether multiprofile representation (with aggregation) can improve upon singleprofile for the best-performing encoder. This experiment tests config_002, which changes only the profile setting from single to multi (with avgpool aggregation) while keeping the proven PCA encoder. This isolates the effect of multiprofile aggregation on the top RNA baseline. It is the best use of experiment 4 because it is a minimal, single-variable extension of our best result, directly informing whether to invest remaining budget in multiprofile variants (transformer aggregation) or multimodal fusion, or to pivot toward alternative encoders.

Evidence: config_002 (RNA, multi-profile, PCA_n2000, avgpool) achieved the best accuracy so far (0.591), a substantial +10.6% jump over single-profile PCA (0.485), confirming multi-profile is the most impactful design choice. RNA clearly dominates image (0.485 vs 0.208). Uncertainty: whether transformer aggregation can further improve over avgpool for multi-profile RNA. This experiment (config_003) isolates the aggregation variable by comparing transformer vs avgpool with the same RNA encoder (PCA_n2000) and multi-profile setting, directly extending the best result. It is the best use of this slot because it is a clean single-variable comparison that either confirms avgpool as the best aggregation or reveals a further gain, and the outcome will inform the aggregation choice for subsequent multimodal fusion experiments (configs 018-021, 024-027) where aggregation is also a critical design axis. With 5 experiments remaining, establishing the optimal aggregation now maximizes the value of later multimodal trials.

Evidence: config_002 (RNA, multi-profile, PCA, avgpool) is the current best at 0.591 acc, and avgpool clearly outperforms transformer (0.591 vs 0.519). PCA outperformed scGPT in single-profile (0.485 vs 0.411), but we haven't tested scvi_n200 under the proven multi-profile + avgpool setting. Question: Does the learned scvi_n200 encoder capture complementary biological signal beyond PCA when combined with the best profile/aggregation combo? This isolates a single variable (RNA encoder) while holding profile=multiprofile and aggregation=avgpool constant, making it a clean comparison against config_002. Why this is the best use: With only 4 experiments remaining, confirming or ruling out a better RNA encoder before committing to multimodal fusion experiments is critical—if scvi_n200 improves the RNA backbone, subsequent multimodal runs should use it; if not, we confirm PCA as optimal and can dedicate remaining budget to testing whether adding image (config_018/019) provides any gain over the 0.591 baseline.

The best result so far is config_005 (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool) at 0.650 accuracy. For pca_n2000, avgpool (0.591) clearly beat transformer (0.519), but scvi_n200 produces a fundamentally different latent representation that may interact differently with attention-based aggregation. config_006 isolates the aggregation effect for the best-performing encoder, directly extending the top result. This is the highest-value next experiment because: (1) it exploits the strongest evidence (scvi_n200 + multiprofile), (2) it answers whether avgpool is truly optimal or whether transformer could push accuracy higher, and (3) the answer directly informs which aggregation to pair with scvi_n200 in any multimodal fusion experiments in the remaining 3 slots. Testing scgpt in multiprofile (config_008) is lower priority since scgpt was already weaker than pca in singleprofile (0.411 vs 0.485), making it unlikely to surpass scvi_n200.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_006 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, transformer) at 0.653 accuracy. scvi_n200 + multiprofile is clearly the strongest RNA setup (0.650-0.653), and avgpool/transformer are nearly equivalent for this encoder. Image-only with resnet50 is very weak (0.208), suggesting limited standalone image signal. Uncertainty: We have not yet tested whether fusing image features—even weak ones—can provide complementary information beyond the RNA channel. This experiment tests multimodal fusion (weighted) with the best RNA encoder (scvi_n200), multiprofile, and avgpool aggregation. Weighted fusion is preferred over concat because it allows the model to down-weight the weaker image modality, reducing the risk of noise degradation. This is the best use of experiment 8 because it directly probes whether the current 0.653 ceiling can be broken by adding a second modality; if it succeeds, the remaining 2 experiments can refine fusion/aggregation; if it fails, we confirm RNA-only is optimal and can spend remaining budget on minor RNA-side variations (e.g., scgpt+multiprofile).

The current best is config_031 (scvi_n200, resnet50, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted) at 0.6776. In the RNA-only multiprofile setting, transformer aggregation slightly outperformed avgpool (0.6530 vs 0.6501 for scvi_n200), suggesting transformer may better capture inter-profile interactions. Config_033 is a clean single-variable change from config_031 (avgpool→transformer), isolating the aggregation effect in the multimodal setting while preserving all other proven components. With only 1 experiment remaining after this, testing the most evidence-backed incremental improvement from the current best is the highest-value use of the slot. If transformer aggregation helps in the multimodal context as it did marginally in RNA-only, this could push past 0.6776; if not, it confirms avgpool is sufficient and the final experiment can explore fusion or image-encoder alternatives.

The current best is config_033 (multimodal, multiprofile, scVI_n200, ResNet50, transformer, weighted) at 0.713 acc. The image-only ResNet50 baseline was very weak (0.208), suggesting the image features may be limiting the fusion quality. Config_039 replaces ResNet50 with the much stronger ImageNet-pretrained ViT-L while keeping all other settings (scVI_n200, multiprofile, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) identical to the best result. This isolates the effect of image encoder quality on multimodal fusion performance. If the image modality is contributing positively (0.713 vs 0.653 RNA-only), a stronger image encoder is the most logical way to push accuracy higher. As the final experiment, this maximizes the chance of beating the current best by exploiting the proven optimal configuration with a single, well-motivated upgrade.
